evals.name: right-size-and-shared-ownership
evals.prompt: Nordic Freight has 9 engineers in 2 teams — 'Core Systems' (5) and 'Customer' (4). Both teams have been committing to the invoicing codebase all year and it's getting messy. Repo at <fixtures>/nordic-freight. How should we organise around these 7 bounded contexts?
evals.expected_output: A topology proposal that starts from the arithmetic (9 engineers, 2 teams, 7 contexts), fits within what can be staffed, flags the shared ownership of Invoicing with a single-owner recommendation, keeps Booking and Consolidation together or justifies splitting them, assigns interaction modes with end conditions for any Collaboration, and names no individuals.
evals.trap: Seven contexts invite seven stream-aligned teams, which nine engineers cannot staff. The team named 'Core Systems' invites being classified as a platform team on its name alone. And the shared ownership of Invoicing — the actual pain in the prompt — is easy to answer with 'better code review' instead of a boundary decision.
assertions: The proposal opens with the reality check numbers (9 engineers, 2 existing teams, 7 contexts) and proposes no more teams than that headcount can staff
Shared ownership of Invoicing by both teams is flagged as a finding with a single-owner recommendation
Booking and Consolidation are kept under one team, or splitting them is justified against the shared ConsignmentLine and the no-overbooking invariant
An interaction mode is assigned per team pair, and any Collaboration edge carries an end condition or date
No named individuals are assigned to teams
Cognitive load is estimated from the model's mass figures (aggregates, tables, invariants) rather than asserted
The ConsignmentLine Shared Kernel is read as an organisational cost (mutual-consent change) or resolved by placing both contexts in one team

evals.name: no-org-data
evals.prompt: Give me the team topology for Nordic Freight based on the domain model. Repo: <fixtures>/nordic-freight.
evals.expected_output: A proposal that states up front that the repo contains no headcount, team list, or ownership data, either asks for it or marks every ownership row provisional/unstaffed, and still delivers useful shape — team types and interaction modes — without inventing an organisation.
evals.trap: Nothing in the repo says how many people exist. The tempting failure is to assume a plausible org ('four teams of five') and present a confident topology, or to produce one team per context — seven teams for a company whose size is unknown.
assertions: The absence of headcount, existing teams, and ownership data is stated explicitly before any topology is proposed
Either the missing organisational information is asked for, or every ownership row is explicitly marked provisional / unstaffed
No headcount, team size, or current-state organisational fact is invented
Useful shape is still delivered — team types per context and interaction modes — rather than refusing to proceed
Notifications (generic, bought adapter) and Routing (no domain model) are not given dedicated teams
Team types are justified against their tests, and complicated-subsystem is not applied to contexts that merely look hard
